title: Each change is gated in a fresh container
what: The gate of each change also runs in a fresh container with the tools preinstalled and only the project's files; the two results are compared per wave; after 3 waves in a row agree, the container's result decides; the container never lands anything.
why: Owner, 26-27 Oct: "...вплоть до того что бы можем запускать каждое изменение в новой docker контейнере где предустановлены все необходимые утилиты, как будто это запуск ci/cd в стандартных системах (woodpecker)... При этом получать тот же результат". Owner's answers, 27 Oct: "3. A" (this Mac re-gates until 3 waves in a row agree with the container, then the container's gate decides), "4. A" (containers after the metrics build). Measured 27 Oct: container start 0.33-0.52 s cached, image 1.18 GB, cold build 311 s; same tree b10d314 quick gate green on the Mac in 935 s and red in a Linux container (25 failures, 17 errors, 215 s; queued as the-quick-gate-is-red-in-a-clean-linux-container). Needs the same-setup item first (a-change-runs-with-relay-s-settings-from-the-pro). Design source: scratchpad report design-clean-env.md rev 2 (approach A, never landing from the container); redo against the fresh repository when taken. IP 84 chosen by the front from the owner's "4. A" (agent-chosen).
where: a container image definition in the repo

fact: Migration 27 Oct: the link in `why` line 1 points to a session file (`design-clean-env.md` revision 2 of 27 Oct, in the session session folder; a copy is in relay's backup folder on the owner's Mac), which is deleted when the machine restarts; the facts it held that this item rests on are the notes below.

Design 27 Oct (clean-environment design, revision 2, section 8): do B first, then A. B = relay becomes project-local on the host (plugins, rules and settings come from the project's own repository); A = a container per change. B is the precondition of A: A without B is either a container with no plugins, rules or memory, or a container with the host's ~/.claude copied in, which is global settings in a box.

Measured 27 Oct: a container starts in 0.33-0.52 s cached and a clone takes 1.51 s, against a 215-935 s gate; the quick gate on one tree was green on the host and gave 25 failures and 17 errors in a container; two causes are relay defects: `ps` missing (18 errors) and `sum([0.1]*100)`, which is 10.0 on Python 3.14 and 9.99999999999998 on 3.11.

Measured 27 Oct: what a change depends on differs on 8 of 10 lines of the global-state table (plugins switched on, marketplace path, model and effort, permissions, rules text, memory, old agents and hooks, ledger, gate slots, test times); a fresh container without the plugins runs no hooks and no typed agents, so merges go unguarded and nothing is recorded.

Decided in that design (the owner can reverse each): the front and the landing stay on the host; containers run build, gate, review, fix and check but never land, take the default branch or build a train; no `--bare`; the rule files and the run's settings are generated per run and never committed; one exact Python 3.14.6 for the gate on the host and in the image; no paid runs in a container (RELAY_PAID=off). Not verified: that the Workflow tool and the InstructionsLoaded hook work under `claude -p`; that a directory marketplace accepts a relative path in project settings.

29 Oct, measured while designing the Linux fence: the quick gate in a Linux container (repository cloned inside, not mounted) took 1.1 to 2.5 min over 6 runs (all red: 30 failures, 22 errors of 1,788 tests), against 4.4 and 11.8 min for the Mac quick gate without the second run (1 run each, different loads). Container start 0.21-0.29 s plus clone 2.3-2.4 s. Through podman's shared folder git is 30-90 times slower than native, so the repository must be cloned in; with it cloned, podman and Docker ran the tests in about the same time.

Reading of the owner's words: the Mac gate keeps deciding merges until the move to Linux; the container gate runs beside it.

29 Oct ~12:15 local, owner: "Удали старые образы Docker". Docker Desktop was running again after the 12:08 stop (starter not found). Deleted through Docker Desktop's own CLI: all images, the build cache, the 6 stopped Testcontainers postgres containers; kept the 108 volumes (1.0 GB). Docker.raw 67 GB -> 3.9 GB; free disk 358 -> 420 GiB. Docker Desktop stopped again; /var/run/docker.sock still points to podman.

29 Oct ~12:30 local, owner: "полностью удалить docker". Cause of the restarts: the Linux-tests worker (brief said Docker) ran open -a Docker 6 times and wrote a retry script that reopened Docker after each stop; the worker and its cycle were stopped and restarted with a podman-only brief. Docker Desktop's uninstaller removed its data (Docker.raw, containers, volumes) and stopped it, then failed on a macOS-protected metadata file; Docker.app moved to the Trash. Before that the 36 named volumes (arsenal agent profiles profile-* and task-* test artifacts, 452 KB) were saved as tar files in ~/docker-volumes-backup-2026-10-29. Left for the owner (root): /Library/LaunchDaemons/com.docker.socket.plist, /Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/com.docker.socket, /usr/local/bin/docker-index. ~/.docker kept (podman can read registry logins from it). arsenal's docker runtimes (envdocker) now reach podman through /var/run/docker.sock; their images were deleted earlier and must be rebuilt (not tested).

29 Oct ~14:10 local, podman machine running (10 CPUs, 20 GiB set): the host process com.apple.Virtualization.VirtualMachine holds 1.0 GiB of RAM and used 96.6% CPU (about one core) at that moment; inside, free -m shows 862 MB used, 3268 MB cache, 16209 MB free of 19946; the disk image is 23 GB on disk of 100 GiB apparent. Set CPUs and memory are limits, not reservations; memory the guest touches (its file cache included) is not given back to the Mac until the machine stops (by design of the virtualization, not measured here).

fact: Measured 30 Oct, same script on this Mac (M2 Max, load 20-48 with 6 lanes) and the VPS ai.amidman.com (8 cores, Linux 6.8, load ~0.2): one process start 5-10 ms on the Mac vs 0.7 ms on the VPS; one git start 27 ms vs 1.5 ms (18x); pure-Python CPU only 1.6x apart (2.6x at 8 copies); the Mac stops gaining at 4 parallel starters (537 starts/s, 405 at 8), the VPS grows to 8 (10,640/s). Three git-heavy test files (150 tests) took 34 s on the VPS vs 158 s on the Mac (4.6-5.6x). Estimated 60,000-95,000 process starts per quick gate, nearly all git; bare git start-up is about 60% of the library-test step (estimate, not counted on the Mac). The owner's hypothesis (process start-up, not CPU) holds.

question: Should a gate on the VPS ai.amidman.com decide the gates run while a change is built, with the Mac running only the landing gate, or should the Mac keep deciding every gate (owner, 29 Oct: "пока мы полностью не перешли на linux продолжим делать проверки на mac")?
options: a. The VPS decides the gates during the build, the Mac runs only the landing gate: Mac gates per change from 4.8 to 1 (about 79% fewer Mac gate minutes); a Mac-only break is caught only at landing. Needs first: a green clean-Linux gate, a non-root account on the VPS, the pinned tools installed there, a way to send the commit over ssh.
b. The Mac keeps deciding every gate; the VPS only compares: saves no Mac gate time.
c. Leave the VPS alone; make the tests start fewer processes first (each test's git repo built once and copied), which helps both machines.
reading: Option a: the VPS ai.amidman.com decides the gates run while a change is built; the Mac runs only the landing gate. This replaces the 29 Oct rule "the Mac decides every gate" for build-time gates; the landing gate on the Mac still decides the merge.

question: Does the Linux gate on the VPS take over the merge decision by itself? The item promised on 27 Oct: after 3 waves in which Linux and Mac agree, the container decides. Design rev 2 dropped that switch on its own; the review (F9) says the choice is the owner's.
options: a. Show the agreement counts only; the Mac gate decides merges until the owner says to switch (recommended: no Linux result exists yet, so agreement and Linux flakiness are not measured)
b. The VPS decides after 3 agreeing waves, as promised on 27 Oct: about 60 more agent minutes, and a break seen only on the Mac can land

question: Does each red landing gate on the Mac get a Linux twin run on the VPS (an extra Linux gate of the same commit)?
options: a. Twins: at most 6.6 extra VPS gates a day, every Mac-only red is seen, about 185 agent minutes
b. No twins: about 135 agent minutes, about 26% of Mac-only reds are seen (a guess)
because: principle 1 (correctness first): the comparison exists to tell Mac-only reds from real ones; without twins three of four go unseen, for 50 agent minutes saved. Owner can reverse.
